title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
why_read: An interesting empirical look at whether autonomous coding agents can design effective semi-supervised learning pipelines when labeled data is scarce, including a new benchmark for program selection.
analysis: AgentSSL studies machine-learning engineering agents operating under semi-supervised conditions, where most data lacks labels, a realistic but underexplored setting compared to the fully labeled benchmarks these agents are usually tested on. The agents managed to beat strong human-engineered baselines in most of the twelve tested settings, but a key weakness emerged: picking which generated program to trust based on the agent's own feedback signal caused big performance drops. The authors address this by releasing ProgramSelectBench, a large benchmark of agent and human SSL programs for studying program selection methods. This is a useful, concrete contribution to understanding the current limits of AI agents doing real ML engineering work.
